prompt_text: I need a personal injury lawyer in Dallas after a truck accident. Which specific law firms should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for a truck accident case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — first, two quick questions so I give the best recommendations:
- Where in Dallas were you (ZIP or neighborhood)?
- Do you want a large national firm with lots of resources or a smaller local firm that handles fewer cases personally?

If you want names right now, call a mix of well‑known Texas plaintiffs’ firms that handle truck crashes plus at least one strong local boutique. Reasons to contact these types of firms are also listed below.

Specific firms to consider (good starting places)
- Morgan & Morgan — national plaintiff firm with large resources, frequently handles catastrophic truck cases and can quickly retain experts (accident reconstruction, trucking-industry consultants, life-care planners). Good if you need big investigative resources.
- Fears Nachawati (Dallas office) — Dallas-based plaintiffs firm known for high-value personal injury and catastrophic cases; strong trial experience and local courtroom familiarity.
- Jim Adler (“The Texas Hammer”) — long-standing Texas personal injury practice; widely known for truck and auto cases and consumer-facing intake that can get you prompt attention.
- Thomas J. Henry Trial Lawyers — large Texas plaintiff firm with nationwide reach and experience in trucking litigation and obtaining large settlements/verdicts.
- Arnold & Itkin LLP — major plaintiffs’ litigation firm (Texas-based attorneys) known for handling complex, high-stakes injury cases and investing in heavy investigation and expert work.

Why call those (and what to expect)
- Truck cases require technical investigation (FMCSA records, ELD/black‑box data, driver logs, maintenance records). Larger firms can get these quickly.
- You want experience with commercial carriers, insurer tactics, and willingness to go to trial if needed — ask about trial verdicts.
- Local firms bring knowledge of Dallas courts, judges, and juries; national firms bring financial and expert resources. Calling both types gives perspective.

What to ask when you call (so you can compare firms)
- Do you handle truck accidents? How many in the last 12 months?
- Who will handle my case (attorney name) and who will be my day‑to‑day contact?
- Have you tried truck cases to verdict? Can you give examples of past results (without violating confidentiality)?
- Will you advance case costs and experts or require me to pay out of pocket?
- What is your contingency fee and any other fees I should expect?
- How long do you expect the case to take and what are likely next steps?
- Do you have experience with FMCSA/ELD/black box evidence and accident reconstruction experts?

What to bring to the first consult
- Police report, photos of the crash and your injuries/vehicle, names and contact info of witnesses, any medical records or bills you already have, your insurance info, correspondence with insurers, and your notes about the crash (time, weather, statements).

Immediate practical steps (before you call or while you wait)
- Get medical care right away and keep records.
- Preserve evidence: photos, damaged clothing, vehicle parts, and your phone video.
- Don’t give recorded statements to the trucking company’s insurer; you can give a statement to your own insurer but limit details and consult counsel first.
- Note the truck company name, DOT number, license plate, driver name if you have it.

If you want, tell me your ZIP code and whether you prefer a big firm or a local boutique and I’ll give a tailored list of 4–6 Dallas firms (with phone numbers and short reasons) to call next.
